subject: Terminal Delight supports repeatable custom skin authoring through one settings file, native evidence and a portable skill
reader: Parker requested and approved this architecture. He knows Terminal Delight, Chalk, OPS and the sibling inventory and wants results and scoped proof without reading Rust.

sections.heading: Your next TD surface starts with one file.
sections.text:
An agent can now create a personal Terminal Delight skin by editing one settings file. These native captures use one build and two files: Chalk keeps its handwriting and cotton stock; Field Notes uses instrument lettering, quieter grain and a glass terminal. The sibling’s OPS work remains part of that same system. 
Implementation review · 20 October 2026 · about four minutes, with the full inventory folded below. Native screenshots are embedded; comments save into this file.

sections.heading: The decisions now meet in the skin.
sections.text:
Application code names a choice, action, caption, meter or frame and keeps its input handlers. Material painting stays behind that shared interface. Font scale, leading and minimum size are independent settings. Notes and terminal glass/stock have explicit policies. 
 02 · The authoring path, built up 

Step 1 · Resolve one file

Step 3 · Export contract and evidence 

 Your TOML Palette recipes · type · material 
 Resolved Skin Existing registry and resolver 
 Native controls Handlers and semantic data stay here 
 Material renderer Stock · grid · plain 
 Catalogue + proof Owners · fixtures · scoped receipts 
 td-skin skill Export · author · inspect · restore 
 The skill reads the running binary’s contract. The diagrams describe the implemented code: the file reader and live settings registry resolve the file; shared helpers dispatch painting; the binary exports the catalogue and matching capture runner. Grey boxes show what each earlier step has not added. 

The existing shape strategies remain finite: a file can combine supported effects. A new silhouette or rendering effect still needs one engine contribution. Terminal cells, authored document bodies, media and semantic state colours retain their own owners.

sections.heading: The native review caught what tests missed.
sections.text:
The first Subscriptions capture failed: the agent wall behind it kept registering its smaller backdrop mask, clipping the wider panel’s edges. The foreground panel now owns that mask. A later capture also caught a paper action backing hiding the bug-report labels; material layers are now added before their content. The failed receipts remain separate from corrected captures.

Chalk · pale palette · palette choices 

Chalk · native gauges and stock 

Field Notes · document frame and reading rail

sections.heading: A saved edit is checked against the live UI.
sections.text:
04 · Reload, rejection and restoration 
- Valid edit The live registry adopts a distinct test skin. 
- Invalid edit The watcher reports the syntax error and retains the last valid tokens. 
- Exact restore The original bytes and resolved tokens return. 
- Private restart An explicit default selection survives; custom is then restored. 
 The proof restarts only the isolated preview. The receipt records the observed selections. Custom file changes in a normal TD window need no restart. 
terminal-delight skin --catalogue
terminal-delight skin --template chalk
terminal-delight skin --check --skin personal-skin.toml --theme hacker
terminal-delight skin --atlas-script
terminal-delight ctl skin snapshot 
For a particular live window, add its explicit --pid . Preserve its previous file bytes or absence and its explicit/theme-following selection before applying a new look.

sections.heading: What is established, and what remains open.
sections.text:
The integrated default suite passed 2,570 tests and the fallback suite passed 2,523, each with ten ignored. After the final boundary changes, all 36 skin tests and 24 allowance tests passed; both CI Clippy variants passed. The final action-order correction passed Clippy and a release build, and its corrected native capture shows all three labels. The earlier engine commit also passed the complete GitHub CI job. 
 | 
 | Matched private fixture | Idle CPU time | Resident memory at end 
 | chalk-usage | 0.190 s / 10.0 s | 191.5 MiB 
 | field-usage | 0.200 s / 10.0 s | 186.6 MiB 
Performance method: one warmed idle sample per skin, same binary and scene, from Linux process counters. It excludes child hosts and compositor cost. It does not establish a regression bound or zero overhead. The grain atlas remains shared and the material adds no animation timer. 
The 29 captures cover 25 distinct registered scenes. Hover, drag and full keyboard interaction remain unverified, and seven catalogue entries have no dedicated fixture. Each receipt names the static states actually inspected; the remaining inventory facets keep their source-routing status. The existing test-only Clippy warnings are tracked in the linked follow-up.

sections.heading: The next surface starts with the exported contract.
sections.text:
The portable td-skin skill guides reference → TOML → native review → apply and restore. It carries no copied inventory and no Parker-specific monitor, path or credential requirement. The capture runner supplies a visible private-window fallback for another compositor. 
Published and merged as the portable td-skin skill . Local discovery links point to its clean tracked worktree; agent-parity passes for every configured host. 
With hindsight, the inventory, real font measurements and choice/action distinction should have come before the first material rollout. The first broad native review should have happened before calling the surface complete. Those checks now travel with the authoring path.
